name: MNPR Client Portal
author: MNPR Web

sections.description:
You build the website. Your client keeps it up to date.

MNPR Client Portal gives your clients a clean, simple portal at yoursite.com/portal/ where they can add and edit exactly the content you choose, such as events, services, team members, news, opening hours or the text on their About page. They log in, change what they need and log out. They never see wp-admin, so they can’t break the design, install plugins or get lost in menus.

Everything is set up on one Content screen, with no code, no extra plugins and no pages to build. Pick a starter, adjust the pages, lists and fields, add your client as a Portal user, and they’re ready.

A finished portal, not a form kit

  • Ready straight away. The portal has its own login, password reset, dashboard, lists, search and My account page. You don’t build any pages.
  • Branded. Add your client’s logo, choose an accent colour, name the portal and add a message to the login page.
  • Easy for clients. Big clear forms, helpful messages, a “Show on the website” switch for drafts, Live and Draft tags in every list, and it works well on phones.
  • Kept out of wp-admin. Portal users are sent to the portal if they try to reach the dashboard, and the admin bar is hidden for them.

Pages, lists and fields, your way

  • Pages for content that appears once, such as the About page text or a home page intro. Each page gets its own simple form in the portal.
  • Lists for content with many items. Make new lists such as Events or Services, or let clients edit a content type you already have.
  • 20 field types, all free: text, long text, rich text, number, email, web address, phone, dropdown, radio buttons, tick boxes, on/off switch, date, time, date and time, image, gallery, file, video link, group and repeater.
  • Repeaters and groups for price lists, line-ups, opening hours and anything else that comes in rows.
  • Business details for things like the phone number, address, opening hours, logo and social links that appear across the whole site.
  • Two free starters: Small Business (news, services, testimonials, contact details) and Events & News (events, news, galleries, contact details).
  • Add the client’s copy yourself. Fill in a page or Business details from wp-admin on the Content tab, using the same form as the portal.
  • Control who sees what. Choose which roles can use the portal, and optionally let each person see only the entries they added.

Show it on your website, however the site is built

  • Automatically. Each list can add its fields to every item’s own page. Choose which fields appear on the page and which appear in lists.
  • Blocks. “Client Portal list” and “Client Portal field” blocks with live previews.
  • Shortcodes that work in any editor, widget or page builder.
  • Page builders such as Breakdance, Elementor and Bricks can read list fields directly, because values are saved as standard custom fields.
  • Theme templates with simple PHP functions.
  • Copy-ready snippets. Every field has a Copy shortcode button, and each page and list has an “On your website” tab with its shortcodes, field names and PHP, each with a Copy button. Client Portal → Tools has the full reference.

Built in

  • Event search-engine data. Events can include schema.org Event data, so search engines can show dates, venues and ticket links.
  • Coming soon mode. Hide the site behind a simple holding page, or one of your own pages, while it’s built. Logged-in editors and portal users still see the real site, and a private link lets others preview it.
  • Cache clearing. Common caching plugins are cleared when clients save, so changes show straight away.
  • Contact email routing. Send form plugin emails to an address your client manages in Business details.
  • AI agent ready. Set up in minutes, or ask your AI agent to do it for you. On WordPress 6.9 and later, agents connected through the MCP Adapter can set up pages, lists and fields, fill in pages and Business details, and add content. Only administrators can use this, and every change gets the same checks as the admin screens.
  • Export and import setups between sites, plus WP-CLI commands.
  • Translation-ready and accessible, with suggested privacy policy text.

Your content stays yours

Values are stored as normal WordPress post meta and options under the field names you choose. If you ever remove the plugin, your content stays exactly where it is.
sections.installation:
1. In your dashboard, go to Plugins → Add New, search for “MNPR Client Portal”, then install and activate it. Or upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ and activate it.
  2. Go to Client Portal → Content and pick a starter, or start from scratch.
  3. Add the pages, lists and fields the site needs, then click Save changes.
  4. Optional: add a logo, colour and login message under Client Portal → Portal.
  5. Add your client under Users → Add New with the role “Portal user”, and send them to yoursite.com/portal/.
  6. Show the content on your site automatically, with the blocks or shortcodes, or with your page builder. Each page and list’s “On your website” tab on the Content screen has copy-ready snippets.
sections.faq:
Do my clients need a WordPress account?

Yes. Each client gets a normal WordPress user account with the “Portal user” role, so you manage them under Users like anyone else. They log in at /portal/ with their email address or username.

Can portal users get into wp-admin?

No. Portal users are redirected to the portal if they try to open the dashboard, the admin bar is hidden for them, and they can’t make changes through the REST API. Administrators can use both the portal and wp-admin.

Will it change how my website looks?

No. The portal has its own simple design, separate from your theme. On the website, content appears inside your theme wherever you choose to show it.

Does it work with my theme or page builder?

It works with block themes and classic themes. Page builders that can show custom fields (post meta), such as Breakdance, Elementor and Bricks, can display the values directly using each field’s name. The shortcodes work anywhere shortcodes do.

How do I show the fields on a page?

There are four ways: automatic display on each item’s page, the two blocks, shortcodes, or your page builder. On the Content screen, every field has a Copy shortcode button, and each page and list has an “On your website” tab with ready-made shortcodes and field names. Client Portal → Tools has the full reference.

What are the shortcodes?

  • [mnprcp_page page="about" name="intro"] shows a field from a page, such as the About page.
  • [mnprcp_list section="events" show="upcoming"] lists a list’s items. Options: show (all, upcoming, past), layout (list, cards), limit, fields, image, link, empty.
  • [mnprcp_field name="venue"] shows one field of the current item. Add post_id="123" to show it from another item.
  • [mnprcp_site name="phone"] shows a Business details field anywhere.

Can I use it in my theme templates?

Yes. Use mnprcp_the_field( 'venue' ) to print a field of the current item, formatted for the website, or mnprcp_get_field( 'venue' ) to get the raw value. For pages, use mnprcp_the_page_field( 'about', 'intro' ) or mnprcp_get_page_field( 'about', 'intro' ). For Business details, use mnprcp_the_site_detail( 'phone' ) or mnprcp_get_site_detail( 'phone' ). Values are also normal post meta, so get_post_meta() works too.

Can clients upload images and files?

Yes. Images are checked to be real images, and other files must be types WordPress allows. Uploads go into the Media Library, and portal users can only use files they uploaded themselves or files already on the item they’re editing.

Can I let clients edit content types I already have?

Yes. When adding a list, choose “Use an existing content type”. Any existing custom fields with the same names as your portal fields are picked up automatically.

What happens to my content if I delete the plugin?

List items (posts) and their values are always kept. The plugin’s settings, page content and Business details are only removed if you first tick “Also delete the portal setup, appearance settings, page content and Business details” under Client Portal → Tools.

Can an AI agent set it up for me?

Yes, on WordPress 6.9 and later. The plugin registers its own abilities with the WordPress Abilities API, so an AI agent connected to your site through the MCP Adapter plugin can see the setup, apply a starter, add, change and remove pages, lists and fields, fill in pages and Business details, add and edit entries, change the portal’s appearance and switch Coming soon mode. Only administrators can use them. Every change goes through the same checks as the admin screens, anything that removes something needs a confirmation, and content is never deleted: removed pages, lists and fields keep their stored values, and entries go to the bin.

Is it translation-ready?

Yes. All text can be translated, and a translation template is included in the languages folder.
sections.changelog:
1.4.1

  • For developers: a new mnprcp_can_manage_site_details filter decides who can edit Business details in the portal. MNPR Client Portal Pro uses it so Events only logins don’t see Business details.
  • For developers: a new mnprcp_preset_applied action fires after a preset is applied, so add-ons can set up anything else it needs.
  • For developers: a new mnprcp_dashboard_after_groups action prints a section on the portal dashboard, after the groups of cards.

1.4.0

  • New: Pages, for content that appears once, such as the About page text or a home page intro. Each page has its own form in the portal, and its fields show on the site with the new [mnprcp_page] shortcode or mnprcp_the_page_field().
  • New: a redesigned Content screen in wp-admin (formerly Sections & fields). Pages, lists and Business details are listed on the left, with Fields, Content, On your website and Settings tabs on the right. Every field has a Copy shortcode button.
  • New: fill in a page or Business details from wp-admin on the Content tab, using the same form as the portal, so you can add your client’s copy yourself.
  • Changed: Site details is now called Business details. Existing fields, values, [mnprcp_site] and mnprcp_get_site_detail() work as before.
  • Changed: the Client Portal menu now has four items: Content, Portal (how the portal looks and who can log in), Coming soon and Tools. Displaying content has moved to the Content screen’s On your website tab, with a full reference on Tools. Old admin addresses redirect.
  • Improved: a lighter, more modern look across wp-admin and the portal, using one shared set of styles.
  • Improved: the portal menu is grouped into Pages, Lists and Settings. Lists show a Live, Draft or Scheduled tag, open with a click anywhere on the row, and keep Edit, View on website and Delete in a “…” menu.
  • Improved: the portal’s edit form has a side panel with Show on the website, Save, View on website and Delete. On phones, Save stays at the bottom of the screen.
  • Improved: Business details is split into small cards, repeater rows are more compact, My account is in two cards, and saving shows a small “Changes saved.” message.
  • New: a small note about Pro on the Content screen, which can be dismissed. It’s hidden when Pro is active or with the mnprcp_show_go_pro filter.
  • New: AI agent abilities for pages (save-page, remove-page, get-page-content and update-page-content). save-field and remove-field also accept page keys.
  • New: developer hooks mnprcp_portal_nav_group, mnprcp_tools_top, mnprcp_presets_after, mnprcp_portal_screen_after, mnprcp_validate_page, mnprcp_can_manage_page and mnprcp_saved_page_values.
  • Fixed: red buttons that are links in the portal now have white text.

1.3.0

  • New: a redesigned portal dashboard. Content is grouped into clear sections, each card shows how many items there are with a quick Add link, and there’s a Recently updated list and a View website button. Site details has its own Settings row.
  • New: the dashboard can show notices that need the client’s attention, such as orders waiting to be posted.
  • New: a Remove link button in the editor. Toolbar buttons now show which formatting is applied, and the toolbar stays in view on long text.
  • Improved: pasting from Word, Google Docs or a web page keeps paragraphs, bold, italic, lists and links, and removes everything else (headings, fonts, colours, sizes, images and tables), so pasted text matches the site.
  • Improved: formatted text saved in the portal is limited to what the editor toolbar can create. Formatting a developer has already added to an item, such as a heading, is kept. Saving in wp-admin is unchanged.
  • New: developer filters mnprcp_dashboard_items, mnprcp_dashboard_groups, mnprcp_dashboard_group, mnprcp_dashboard_attention and mnprcp_rich_text_allowed_html. The mnprcp_dashboard_cards action still works.

1.2.1

  • New: Client Portal → Go Pro, a short page about the Pro add-on. It’s hidden once Pro is active, and the mnprcp_show_go_pro filter hides it on client sites.
  • Fixed: the update-appearance and update-coming-soon abilities now accept a call with no settings.

1.2.0

  • New: AI agent support. On WordPress 6.9 and later, AI agents (for example through the MCP Adapter) can set up the portal and add content using the plugin’s abilities. Administrators only; every change is checked like the admin screens, and removals need a confirmation.
  • New: developer methods MNPRCP_Config::stored() and MNPRCP_Settings::update(), and the mnprcp_abilities filter for add-ons.
  • Fixed: the post_id shortcode example in the readme showed curly quotes on WordPress.org.

1.1.1

  • Security: setup JSON from the builder, imports and setup files is sanitised as soon as it’s decoded.
  • Security: event data for search engines escapes tags inside its script block.
  • New: Displaying content shows the address to use in a form plugin to send emails to a Site details email field.
  • Fixed: an item with no main image showed a Remove button in the portal.

1.1.0

  • New: Coming soon mode. Hide the website behind a simple holding page (or one of your own pages) while it’s built or worked on, with a maintenance option and a private preview link. The portal keeps working.
  • New: hooks for add-ons (portal screens, portal menu, dashboard cards, admin menu and portal page areas).
  • Improved: presets are grouped by type when add-ons provide more.

1.0.0

  • First public release.
